transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-06-30
- Time: 14:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM); Dr. Aisha Khan (Stelara CTO), Ben Ortiz (Head of ML), Maya Patel (InfoSec), Jordan Lee (Platform)

Summary:
Quick scoping call for a 4-week POC focused on data handling and logging concerns for Stelara Health. Primary goals: define success criteria, workload sizing for benchmarks, what data can be used in tests (PII constraints), logging and redaction requirements, retention/ prompt storage policy, and timeline for trial Dedicated capacity.

Topics: POC goals and success metrics; dataset and PII handling; logging / telemetry / redaction; retention windows; prompt & response storage; workload sizing and expected QPS; benchmark plan; timeline and next steps.

Transcript (timestamps approximate):
[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. we got lucas and priya from the eng team and ethan on CSM. how's everybody doing?
[00:06] Aisha Khan: good thanks, excited to dig in. we got a short agenda from our side - want to make sure we can run a POC that meets our compliance bar.
[00:12] Ben Ortiz: yeah copy, we're mainly trying to validate latency/cost tradeoffs and make sure we never send PII off-network for production. for POC we can use a de-identified sample but want to test redaction behaviors.
[00:20] Lucas Rivera: great, that's exactly what we usually scope. quick question on success criteria do you have quant thresholds? like 95th perc latency, throughput, and quality metrics?
[00:28] Ben Ortiz: target ~95th <= 300ms for 512-token responses, throughput about 30 qps sustained for the workload we gave earlier. quality: F1 on entity extraction > 0.88 and hallucination rate below 3% on our eval set.
[00:44] Priya Nair: ok good, that gives us a baseline. for the POC we'll propose benchmark runs on both Hosted and a short Dedicated trial (reserved pool) so we can show differences in latency SLOs and cost.
[00:56] Maya Patel: i want to focus on data handling. production will be VPC Private deployment, but for the POC do you require customer-managed VPC or can we use hosted with network peering? security concerns drive that.
[01:06] Ethan Cole: we can do either. typical pattern: start with Hosted but lock redaction and retention settings, and for deeper security customers we spin up Private Dedicated in their VPC. for POC we can also do a dedicated tenant with tighter retention and no persistent prompt storage.
[01:18] Jordan Lee: when you say "no persistent prompt storage" what does that mean? do you deterministically purge prompt vectors or do you redact and store?
[01:25] Lucas Rivera: short answer: configurable. Redwood supports three modes: (1) ephemeral-only \u2014 no prompts or responses persisted beyond request lifetime, (2) redacted storage \u2014 we store events but redact tokens or PII fields, and (3) full retention \u2014 store prompt+response for X days. for POC we recommend ephemeral or redacted depending on compliance.
[01:39] Dr. Aisha Khan: can you explain how redaction works? is it client-side or server-side? we need assurance that the redaction removes PHI before any logging reaches third-party services.
[01:48] Priya Nair: we do both options. a common flow: customer applies client-side redaction filters (we'll provide a library) then server-side NLP redaction as a second layer. server-side redaction tags PII with placeholders before anything is written to logs or metrics. redaction heuristics include regex, entity models for names/SSNs/medical IDs, and custom safe-lists.
[02:05] Maya Patel: is the server-side redaction deterministic and auditable? we need logs that show redaction happened w/o the raw PII present.
[02:11] Lucas Rivera: yes, we emit audit events that indicate redaction occurred and what rule matched, but those events do not contain the raw PII. we can produce redaction hashes for traceability if you need to map across systems without revealing the PII.
[02:23] Ben Ortiz: what about model caching and KV cache \u2014 if we have a prefix with patient info in it, could that live in memory on the GPU and be recovered later?
[02:31] Priya Nair: KV cache is ephemeral in the serving runtime and is cleared between sessions if you choose ephemeral; for Dedicated we can guarantee session isolation. we don't persist KV cache to disk unless you explicitly enable session resume (and you'd opt into storage policies).
[02:44] Jordan Lee: ok that helps. on retention window \u2014 what's the granularity? can we set retention to like 7 days for prompt metadata, zero days for full prompt text?
[02:52] Lucas Rivera: yes, retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route. you can set metadata retention longer (e.g., 90 days) but redact or zero-day retention for prompt payloads. for the POC we'll show sample configs: e.g., prompts = 0 days, responses = 7 days redacted, telemetry = 30 days.
[03:10] Aisha Khan: we'd like to stress test the redaction \u2014 if the PII is obfuscated but still reconstructable by model, that could be a leak. do you run any safety checks to detect reconstruction risk?
[03:20] Priya Nair: good call \u2014 we run synthetic reconstruction tests during benchmarks: we feed masked examples and try to recover masked tokens, measure leakage. we also include prompt-scrubbing evaluation in our quality checks.
[03:33] Ben Ortiz: for the POC benchmark we'll need cost estimates. can you give rough per-token or per-request numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:40] Maya Chen: we'll send a pricing note but rough guidance: Hosted is higher per-token but no infra ops; Dedicated has commit pricing with lower per-token compute and predictable throughput. we'll include estimated costs for the benchmark profiles you gave (30 qps sustained, 512 token avg).
[03:55] Jordan Lee: what's the benchmark setup? do you run against a model catalog or a pinned model?
[04:02] Lucas Rivera: we recommend pinning a model version so results are reproducible. for the POC we'll pick a candidate open model from our catalog (we'll propose two: one quantized for cost and one FP16 for quality). we'll run 3 phases: warmup, steady-state throughput, and quality eval on your eval set.
[04:18] Ben Ortiz: how do you handle logging to third-party telemetry like Datadog? we want audit logs but some fields must be omitted.
[04:25] Priya Nair: integrations like Datadog receive only metadata and redaction markers by default. you can enable more detailed logs in an allowlist, but for Stelara we'd recommend an allowlist that excludes prompt_text and response_text.
[04:36] Maya Patel: can we bring our own KMS and have keys in HSM for encryption at rest?
[04:41] Lucas Rivera: yes for Private deployments and Dedicated VPC we support customer-managed keys (KMS + HSM). Hosted can integrate with customer KMS via trusted key wrapping in some configurations \u2014 we'll share the KMS integration guide.
[04:52] Aisha Khan: one more \u2014 data residency. some of our patients are in EU and we need EU data to remain in EU. can POC be done in us-west but with EU-only options?
[05:01] Maya Chen: POC canonical path is run in the region you choose; for EU data we can provision resources in eu-west and run benchmarks there. for initial scoping you can redact and anonymize data and run functional tests in us-west, but perf/latency tests should be run in-region.
[05:15] Ben Ortiz: timeline \u2014 we want a 4-week POC. week 0 is setup and security review, week 1 warmup & integration, week 2 benchmark runs, week 3 evaluation and handoff. does that align?
[05:24] Ethan Cole: yes that's our standard. we'll aim to have Dedicated trial standing by by the end of week 0. we need sample data and signed SOW + any network allowlists to start.
[05:31] Jordan Lee: what about SSO and RBAC for internal reviewers during the POC?
[05:35] Priya Nair: we support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC per route and per-team. for POC we'll create a few roles: admin, reviewer, and observer.
[05:43] Maya Patel: curious about hidden telemetry \u2014 is there any accidental storage of raw prompt in logs we can't control? I've seen vendors where even error traces include snippets.
[05:50] Lucas Rivera: we have a policy to scrub stack traces and error logs before persisting. error breadcrumbs that include user input are redacted by default; there's a knob to include them in a safe-mode for debugging by special request with strict audit.
[06:04] Ben Ortiz: ok sounds good. let's talk about the benchmark itself in detail \u2014 we'll send a representative workload: mix of extraction tasks (60%), summarization (30%), and reranking (10%), avg tokens 512 but some bursts to 1024. can you size the Dedicated pool?
[06:18] Priya Nair: for 30 qps at 512 tokens with p95 <= 300ms we estimate needing a pool of 4xA100-equivalent GPUs with low-latency network; we'll refine after we run initial small-scale tests. Dedicated trial will emulate that and we can scale during the POC.
[06:32] Maya Chen: we will also include intelligent batching suggestions and quantization profile to reach the cost targets. Lucas will own the benchmark run.
[06:39] Lucas Rivera: noted. i'll prepare a runbook \u2014 test phases, metrics to collect (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, tokens/sec, cost-per-token, redaction success rate, leakage tests, and quality metrics you specified).
[06:54] Aisha Khan: finally, acceptance criteria \u2014 if the Dedicated trial meets latency and quality constraints and redaction passes the leakage tests, we'll consider POC succeeded and proceed to procurement.
[07:03] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll wrap that into the SOW.

[07:10] -- Short clarifying Q&A / noise and small talk (~5m) --
[12:10] Ben Ortiz: quick question, if a prompt inadvertently contains PHI, can we configure immediate alerting and automatic deletion?
[12:18] Priya Nair: yes alerting on redaction rule hits is supported; you can route alerts to your pager or to an internal queue. automatic deletion is also supported via retention policies \u2014 we can set zero-day retention for raw prompts and retain only hashed metadata for audit.
[12:30] Jordan Lee: during the benchmark will you run the reconstruction / leakage test against our eval set or synthetic variants?
[12:36] Lucas Rivera: both \u2014 synthetic variants to stress heuristics and your real anonymized eval to validate in situ.
[12:42] Maya Patel: for audit we need a record that redaction took place but never the cleartext. that earlier comment about redaction hashes \u2014 can you show a sample audit row?
[12:51] Lucas Rivera: yes we'll include an example in the docs we send \u2014 row fields: event_id, timestamp, redaction_rule_id, redaction_hash, route, tenant_id, no raw_text.
[12:59] Ben Ortiz: sounds good.

Recap / Next steps:
- Redwood to send SOC2 report, network diagram, KMS guide and redaction sample docs (Maya) - due 2026-07-02.
- Customer to supply anonymized sample dataset, schema, and concrete success criteria (Ben) - due 2026-07-03.
- Redwood to provision Dedicated trial and prepare benchmark runbook (Lucas) - ready by 2026-07-05, run week of 2026-07-06.
- Redwood to send draft POC SOW and pricing (Maya) - due 2026-07-01.

End of call.
